messages:
Anna (CS): Hey team — Seabright returned the vendor security questionnaire. They flagged three net-new blockers: customer-managed keys (BYOK) for embeddings, a shorter embeddings retention window request, and a ask for nightly debug logs. They want answers by EOD Friday. Copying the relevant Qs below.
Miguel (CS): Thanks — can you paste the exact question text?
Anna (CS): Sure. Q1: 'Do you support customer-managed keys for embeddings and associated artifacts?' Q2: 'Can embedding retention be set to 7 days for test tenants?' Q3: 'Can we receive nightly debug logs with request/response ids?'
Alex (Seabright): Hi all — yes those are the asks. Our security team is ok with redacted logs but BYOK and retention are blockers for us going GA.
Kara (CS): Alex — quick clarifying q: BYOK for embeddings only, or for all persisted artefacts including logs/metrics?
Alex (Seabright): Embeddings + any persisted debug dumps. Metrics aggregated ok.
Jonas (Security): Quick answers from the infra side: BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private deployments (customer provides KMS key or HSM), not for Hosted API by default. For Hosted we can provide a KMS attestation and key provenance docs but not give the key.
Priya (Legal): Re BYOK on Hosted — that would require an enterprise addendum (BYOK addendum + tech specs). I can draft the addendum language but need product confirmation on what's technically feasible.
Miguel (CS): I'll fetch the current subprocessor list and any prior addenda. s3://redwood-customer-docs/subprocessors.csv — will share snapshot in this thread when pulled.
doc-bot: Uploaded subprocessor snapshot to internal drive: drive.redwood/seabright/subprocessors_2026-03-18.csv
Jonas (Security): On retention: default embeddings TTL is 30 days for hosted; we can offer 7 days as a special config for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request a shorter retention but it triggers more aggressive cache eviction and may impact performance — I can include a short technical note.
Kara (CS): About logs: we can't export raw PII-containing request/response logs overnight. We can provide support packages: redacted traces with request ids, sampled request headers, and an incident-level export on request. Suggest we offer: redacted nightly dump + a separate forensic-only access window for escalations.
Alex (Seabright): That sounds promising. For BYOK they want explicit confirmation where the key lives and key provenance. Also would accept an attestation for hosted if BYOK isn't possible.
Priya (Legal): I'll draft two canned responses for the questionnaire: (A) Hosted API answer: no BYOK, provide KMS attestation + redacted log export option + retention default 30 days (reduction negotiable as an SOW). (B) Dedicated/Private answer: BYOK supported, retention configurable to 7 days, redacted logs available. I'll include suggested contract language for the BYOK addendum.
Jonas (Security): I'll add a short technical paragraph we can paste into the form: ```Embeddings retention: default 30 days (hosted). For Dedicated/Private, retention TTL is configurable via deployment policy; can be reduced to 7 days upon request. BYOK: supported on Dedicated/Private via KMS/HSM integration; for Hosted we provide key provenance and attestation but do not accept customer keys into shared KMS. Redacted logs: we support redacted nightly exports and per-incident forensic exports.```
Miguel (CS): ETA for subprocessor list: I can have the cleaned CSV and a bullet list of subprocessors by Thu 17:00 PT.
Anna (CS): Plan: Miguel — subprocessor list by Thu 5pm. Jonas — paste the tech snippet into the questionnaire and flag any constraints by Thu noon. Priya — draft two canned legal answers + BYOK addendum language by Thu EOD. Kara — I'll assemble and send back to Alex on Friday morning for internal review.
Alex (Seabright): Can you confirm whether hosted retention can ever be reduced below 30 days, even temporarily for a pilot? Our security lead is pushing for 7 days during POC.
Jonas (Security): For Hosted, temporary reductions are possible but non-trivial — they require cache/eviction tuning and will likely increase token costs. We can offer a timeboxed pilot (7 days) under an engineering change request and SOW. I'll note the operational impacts in our response.
Priya (Legal): Noted. If we do a timeboxed pilot, Legal will want explicit acceptance criteria and a rollback plan in the SOW.
Anna (CS): Sounds good. I'll log actions in the onboarding tracker and set a Friday EOD follow-up. @Alex — we'll aim to get a consolidated form back to you Friday morning. :thumbsup:
Miguel (CS): ACK — I'll upload the subprocessor CSV here once done.
Jonas (Security): ACK — drafting tech blurb now.
Priya (Legal): ACK — will loop in Contracts for the addendum.
Alex (Seabright): Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround.
Anna (CS): Closing notes: next check-in Friday 10:00 PT. If anything blocks earlier, ping this thread.
